title: The reduced geometric fibre locus has a constant open part on each closed stratum
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For each $y\in Y$ use a geometric fibre over a chosen algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-geometric-fibre], and set
$$E_f=\{y\in Y\mid X_{\bar y}\text{ is reduced}\},$$
where reduced means that every local ring has no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. For every irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq |Y|$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], there is a nonempty relatively open subset $V\subseteq Z$ such that either $V\subseteq E_f$ or $V\cap E_f=\varnothing$. Neither $Y$ nor $Z$ is assumed reduced or Noetherian, and neither flatness nor nonemptiness of the fibres is required. Irreducible subsets are nonempty as in the cited definition; the assertion is vacuous when $Y$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0579 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible), second proof paragraph: restriction to an irreducible closed subscheme and the two generic-fibre alternatives; Tags 0577 (lemma-not-geometrically-reduced-in-neighbourhood), 0578 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-generic-fibre), 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced).

proof.text: Fix an irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq |Y|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme], choose a closed immersion $i:T\to Y$ with image $Z$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $i$ is a homeomorphism $|T|\simeq Z$; hence $T$ is nonempty and irreducible. Apply [lem-sc-scheme-sober] to the irreducible closed subset $|T|$ of $T$ to obtain its generic point $\eta$. No reducedness of this chosen scheme structure is needed.

source.place: Tag 0579, lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible, second proof paragraph: choose an irreducible closed subscheme; schemes.tex Tags 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme) and 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: Form $h:X_T=X\times_Y T\to T$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied to $f$ and $i$, says that $h$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation. These are the two finiteness assumptions of the generic-constancy statement. This application does not require the closed immersion $i$ to be finitely presented, or $f$ to be quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 01TS, lemma-base-change-finite-presentation, locally-finite-presentation assertion; schemes.tex Tag 01K5, lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change; restriction in Tag 0579.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-generic-constancy-geometric-reducedness] to $h$ and $\eta$. Obtain a nonempty open $W\subseteq T$ such that, for every $t\in W$, $(X_T)_t$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(t)$ if and only if $(X_T)_\eta$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(\eta)$. By excluded middle on the latter proposition, either all the fibres at $t\in W$ are geometrically reduced, or none are.

source.place: Tag 0579, lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible, second proof paragraph: the alternatives from Tags 0578 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-generic-fibre) and 0577 (lemma-not-geometrically-reduced-in-neighbourhood).

proof.text: Let $E_h=\{t\in T\mid (X_T)_{\bar t}\text{ is reduced}\}$. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-algebraic-closure-test] to the scheme $(X_T)_t$ over $\kappa(t)$, for each $t\in W$. By [def-weil-geometric-fibre], its base change to the chosen algebraic closure is precisely $(X_T)_{\bar t}$. Thus step 3 says either $W\subseteq E_h$ or $W\cap E_h=\varnothing$. The criterion includes empty fibres.

source.place: Tag 035X, lemma-geometrically-reduced, (2) iff (6), and Tag 020I, lemma-perfect-reduced, as assembled in the cited algebraic-closure-test node; geometric-fibre convention in schemes.tex, fibre products.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] for $f$ and $i$, $E_h=i^{-1}(E_f)$. Set $V=i(W)$. The homeomorphism in [def-weil-closed-immersion] shows that $V$ is a nonempty relatively open subset of $Z$. If $W\subseteq E_h$, every $y=i(t)\in V$ belongs to $E_f$. If $W\cap E_h=\varnothing$, a point $y=i(t)\in V\cap E_f$ would give $t\in W\cap i^{-1}(E_f)=W\cap E_h$, a contradiction. These are the required alternatives. If $Y$ is empty there is no nonempty irreducible closed subset to consider.

source.place: Tag 0576, lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced, applied to the closed immersion; Tag 0579, lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible, final paragraph.
